To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) local polymer chain yielding dominates local toughening in neat polymers; (2) local stiffening alone is a net toughening mechanism in neat polymers and can be used to enhance the toughness of polymers; and (3) local yielding and local stiffening can both contribute to local toughening, but the net effect of local stiffening on local toughness is strongly dependent on the particle spacing.

(1) the local toughening mechanisms in the process zone of a propagating crack in a neat polymer are dominated by chain disentanglements and local anisotropic hardenings, and (2) the presence of stiff nanoparticles can either increase or decrease toughness, depending on the balance between the local yielding and local stiffening mechanisms.

(1) the local yielding of the polymer chains is the dominant toughener, (2) local chain stiffening alone decreases toughness, and (3) local yielding is the primary toughener for inclusions, and (4) the toughening effect of inclusions can be optimized by balancing the local stress concentration and local yield zone size.
